It was pretty unanimous that we wanted to do this, so I think it's probably fine to implement it now? <@308223150725005322> brought up an interesting point re EL specs for 4844, re: `blob_versioned_hashes: List[VersionedHash, MAX_VERSIONED_HASHES_LIST_SIZE]` MAX_VERSIONED_HASHES_LIST_SIZE is 2**24, so a single tx can carry a number of VersionedHashes that shoots significantly past the number of blobs that can be included in a block presently, and Presumably a tx cannot be included across multiple blocks, so the EL limit at runtime will always need to be at least the same as the CL limit. I'm guessing this is future proofing so we can raise limits without changing the EIP, with the intent of implementations setting a lower limit at first? Will this always be set to match the CL's `MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK` (=4 currently) param? ah, sorry, this is on me. wanted to just add the 0 blob ban, but realized that the conditions are currently a bit mis-specified in the EIP, and the refactor got stuck. Will merge the minimal 0 blob ban tomorrow to have it in the specs, and then finish up the proper refactor (that's the draft PR) afterwards but yes, decision has already been made to ban 0 blob txs. I'm working through my PR to the execution apis to add datagas to the tx receipt and just wanted to confirm which value we should be reporting in the receipt (`dataGasConsumed` or `dataGasConsumed * feePerDataGas`). I'm assuming we just want `dataGasConsumed` following `gasUsed` but wanted to confirm https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/398 Here's the early draft. I've started a PR on `ethereumjs` to add the data gas field in our client and will work on getting a test generated as well

excerpts.author: __kasey__
excerpts.content:
<@308223150725005322> brought up an interesting point re EL specs for 4844, re:
`blob_versioned_hashes: List[VersionedHash, MAX_VERSIONED_HASHES_LIST_SIZE]` MAX_VERSIONED_HASHES_LIST_SIZE is 2**24, so a single tx can carry a number of VersionedHashes that shoots significantly past the number of blobs that can be included in a block presently, and Presumably a tx cannot be included across multiple blocks, so the EL limit at runtime will always need to be at least the same as the CL limit. I'm guessing this is future proofing so we can raise limits without changing the EIP, with the intent of implementations setting a lower limit at first? Will this always be set to match the CL's `MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK` (=4 currently) param?
